content.text: Let me test the byte-size boundary and whitespace handling:

arguments.command:
cd /app/tmp && python3 - << 'EOF'
import json, subprocess, sys
base = json.dumps({"mode":"burst","banks":2,"lanes":2,"limit":10,"borders":[0,5,10],
                   "start_bank":0,"packets":[{"id":"a","lane":0,"rank":1}]}).encode()
# pad with whitespace to just under 24 MiB
pad = b' ' * (24*1024*1024 - 1 - len(base) - 1)  # + newline
data = pad + base + b'\n'
print("size", len(data), "<= 24MiB:", len(data) <= 24*1024*1024)
r = subprocess.run([sys.executable,"-I","-B","/app/submission/scheduler.py"], input=data, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
print("just-under rc", r.returncode, r.stdout[:60])
# just over
data2 = pad + base + b'\n' + b' '
print("size2", len(data2))
r2 = subprocess.run([sys.executable,"-I","-B","/app/submission/scheduler.py"], input=data2, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
print("just-over rc", r2.returncode, r2.stdout[:60])
# leading whitespace + tabs/newlines
data3 = b'\n\t  ' + base
r3 = subprocess.run([sys.executable,"-I","-B","/app/submission/scheduler.py"], input=data3, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
print("leading-ws rc", r3.returncode, r3.stdout[:40])
EOF
